prompt: Talk trash to the Soviet space program. The Space Race is over. Rub it in.
response:
The Soviet space program had some legendary firsts—Sputnik, Gagarin, Luna—but if we’re talking Space Race bragging rights: the finish line had bootprints on the Moon, and they weren’t wearing CCCP patches.

They sprinted out of the gate, made the world panic, then watched NASA go from “we should probably learn rockets” to “we parked a car on the Moon” in a decade. The N1 rocket tried to answer Saturn V and mostly answered with “kaboom.” Four launches, four failures—less a Moon rocket, more a state-funded fireworks subscription.

By 1969, the USSR was still trying to make a lunar landing program happen while Apollo 11 was busy turning the Moon into an American historical landmark. The Space Race wasn’t a photo finish; it was the U.S. planting a flag while the Soviet lunar program pretended it had never really wanted to go anyway.

So yes: Sputnik beeped first. Gagarin flew first. But when the biggest trophy was “humans on the Moon,” the Soviet program was stuck on Earth, listening to Houston take the victory lap.
